Definition: to be (causatively, make) lofty, especially inaccessible; by implication, safe, strong; used literally and figuratively
BiblicalUsage: In Hebrew, sâgab means to be (causatively, make) lofty, especially inaccessible; by implication, safe, strong. In Deuteronomy 2:36, we read, "…Gilead, there was not one city too strong…"; in Isaiah 2:11, "The lofty looks of man shall be humbled…". You hear it again in Job 5:11 — "…low; that those which mourn may be exalted…" — and in Proverbs 18:10, "…the LORD a strong tower: the righteous runneth…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word sâgab is in the Bible for a reason, and it carries weight far beyond its size in the text. And I hold that sâgab is as true now as when it was first written, because God does not change.
